stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Windhorst on the Gary Trent Jr. situation in Milwaukee: "I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league. You know, they're like, 'Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation? Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation?' It is being done by a different law firm than did the Clippers investigation. They were sort of twin investigations.

"I will just say I was talking to an executive the other day and he just said if this was a pre-existing deal and let's just be honest, the word of this deal was out there in the spring. I had an executive say to me that they think, and I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but I had an executive say to me, if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers deal. When you think of it, the Clippers didn't get any salary cap relief for their salary cap circumvention. They were just funneling their max player more money.

In the case of the Bucks, allegedly Gary Trent signed back-to-back minimum contracts and then got this $64 million deal. And over these last two years as they were trying to hang on to Giannis Antetokounmpo for dear life, they got that flexibility that they were able to put into the roster. It didn't work.

"Well, I'm just saying if you're going to compare it to Joe Smith ... this is more comparable to what happened with Joe Smith if indeed they are found guilty."

Slater on a Porzingis' status in Golden State: "He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp. He went to this event with Jimmy Butler in San Diego, but if you talk to players and people at that event, he wasn't getting on the court. He wasn't in the weight room. He would show up to more of the dinners and the fun stuff.

"But it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with this health issue and thinking about his future. He calls Mike Dunleavy the day before training camp, basically tells him he's not coming in to work, he's going to go deal with this health thing.

"He showed up for one meeting two weeks into camp as the Warriors team was in Las Vegas. He met with Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini. From my understanding, those are pretty much the only two he's been communicating with during this entire process. After that meeting, the Warriors announced that he was going to be around the team. Then he left the facility and hasn't returned and has not been around the team to the point that when we put out the report yesterday, the Warriors didn't address some of the trade speculation, but did say he will not be around the team in the immediate future.

"Clearly, this is something, as you mentioned, that Mike Dunleavy's called around the league and explored."

Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal
Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return.

Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season.

Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks

Sources: Warriors begin exploring trades for Porzingis

The Golden State Warriors have begun the process of looking for trades for center Kristaps Porzingis, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Porzingis remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has had him questioning his future with basketball.

If there isn't a breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from his career is possible, sources told Charania.

Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion.

"Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure that it's the right partners because they're now partners with us. And the right value, but also are they doing the right things for the fans? I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle's one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. The NBA is a global game. And so having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I mean, can you go that many more? So, it's like, can you grow? Can you cover a big market like Vegas?

"I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it."

Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside.

"There's also no tanking. So there's not five free wins, eight free wins. And in the East last year, a lot of teams really compounded that because there was about seven teams, six teams trying to lose, which is horrible for our game. NBA Adam Silver did a great job. We got rid of that. So there's no tanking.

"People are going to win -- 45 wins is a hell of a season. And I think it's going to be very, very tough. And I think that might be a 4, 5, 6 seed where last year it was 50, 52 wins to get to that level. And so, I think that's not been talked about enough."

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

The ramifications of the Hukporti injury for Philadelphia
The season ending Achilles injury to Ariel Hukporti has roster ramifications for the 76ers.

The 76ers do have an open two-way spot and can sign a player with three years or less in service.

Doncic, who 'worked his butt off all summer,' lights up Kings
A lighter Luka Doncic scored an easy 21 first-half points in the Los Angeles Lakers' preseason opener over the Sacramento Kings on Monday night, needing only 16 minutes to sharpen up his game in a 127-103 blowout in Sacramento.
Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious.

"The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape."

The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws.

"For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm."

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

stories.headline: Fever president Kelly Krauskopf steps down after 2nd stint
stories.summary: Fever president Kelly Krauskopf, who oversaw the team as it made the playoffs for 12 consecutive seasons, has stepped down from her position.
stories.body:
Indiana Fever president Kelly Krauskopf has stepped down from her position, the team announced Friday.

"It has been an honor and a privilege to help build and steward the Indiana Fever with the support and trust of [owner] Herb Simon," Krauskopf said in a statement. "I am deeply grateful for the opportunities, relationships, and shared accomplishments that have shaped my time with this organization. The Fever is poised for an exciting future, and I am proud to have helped lay the foundation for its continued growth and success."

Krauskopf said she informed the team of her decision before the end of the season.

She was the hired as president and general manager prior to the franchise's inaugural 2000 season and oversaw the organization as it made the playoffs for 12 consecutive years, advanced to three WNBA Finals and won the championship in 2012. In 2018, Krauskopf transitioned to the Indiana Pacers as assistant general manager and became the first woman in NBA history to hold an executive basketball management role.

Krauskopf returned to the Fever as president of basketball and business operations in 2024.

"When we started the Fever, Kelly saw what this franchise could become," Simon said in a statement. "She built it, delivered a championship and came back when we needed her. She has played an extraordinary role in the growth of women's basketball in Indianapolis, and our family is grateful for everything she's given this organization. I'm proud to call her a friend."

stories.summary: Michael Carrick has refused to rule out dropping Bruno Fernandes for Bournemouth's visit to Old Trafford on Sunday after the Manchester United captain appeared to criticise his tactics following the defeat to Como.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick has refused to rule out dropping Bruno Fernandes for Bournemouth's visit to Old Trafford on Sunday after the Manchester United captain appeared to criticise his tactics following the defeat to Como.

Fernandes revealed in a post-match TV interview it was the decision of Carrick and his staff not to press Como man-for-man and suggested it had contributed to the heavy 4-1 defeat.

Speaking at a news conference on Friday, Carrick was asked whether he would consider dropping Fernandes or stripping him of the captaincy in the wake of his comments, but the United head coach chose to dodge the question.

"The most important thing for me is the team, first and foremost," said Carrick

"It's the squad, it's the dynamics in the squad. And again, it's about the football club. And I'll always do what's best for the football club."

Pushed on whether he had thought about removing Fernandes as captain, Carrick replied: "I'm just saying I'll always, whatever the situation is, I'll always do what's best for the football club."

He also refused to reveal anything about conversations between the pair since the game in Como.

"If I've spoken to him or haven't spoken to him, I don't think this is the time to go into too much detail," sald United boss

- Transfer rumors, news: Como's Paz destroyed Man United -- now they want to sign him

Fernandes is the second player to turn his fire on staff in as many weeks after Lisandro Martínez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the board.

It has prompted questions about divisions in the dressing room, but Carrick insists players and staff are on the same page.

"It's not divided, no, it's not divided," he said.

"We just need to get back to doing what we do best, and we will. We need to move forward in the right direction for sure. We need to do things to enable us to do that. So, it's pretty clear."

stories.headline: After two opposite fights, what should be expected from Yan vs. Dvalishvili 3
stories.summary: Merab Dvalishvili has tweaked his fight plan, while Yan has gone all-in on his. Which strategy will win out?
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- The UFC Performance Institute is nearly empty as Merab Dvalishvili wraps up his final round of sparring on a Saturday afternoon. He has been going for hours, switching among three partners after each five-minute round. Except for Dvalishvili's team, the place is deserted -- not because it's a slow day, but because it's technically closed. UFC staff was meant to clean and lock the doors 30 minutes ago, but Dvalishvili's workout is running long (as they tend to do). At this moment, though, the session appears finished. Coaches have turned their backs to the cage, and teammates are packing up their bags.

Then suddenly, a bell sounds and Dvalishvili walks out for another round of work. His seventh.

"I don't even know," head coach John Wood says when asked the maximum number of rounds he's ever witnessed Dvalishvili spar at once. "Just the other day he did 10, and I swear he could have done five more. We're not talking fluff rounds, either. We're talking 10 rounds, hard as f---.

"I really don't know who does that."

It could be that no one else does that. It's fair to wonder whether sparring 10 rounds at a time -- impressive as it might be -- is even a good idea. Such is the predicament of Merab "The Machine" Dvalishvili.

Dvalishvili pushed the limits of MMA history in 2025. He successfully defended the UFC's bantamweight championship three times in a span of 10 months, then attempted an unprecedented fourth title defense in a single calendar year in December. Dvalishvili ultimately fell short, losing his belt to Petr Yan in a five-round decision at UFC 323. Dvalishvili (21-5) will seek to recapture the belt when he faces Yan (20-5) for a third time Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (main card begins at 2 p.m. ET).

No UFC fighter has ever defended a title four times in a year, and none had even tried before Dvalishvili -- for good reason. To even attempt it, Dvalishvili had to walk a fine line between ambitious and foolish. He cut weight twice in 63 days for the December fight and concealed a significant knee injury from members of his team after UFC physicians told him he should consider withdrawing from the bout.

"Everything went bad," Dvalishvili admitted to ESPN. "I had the worst game plan, worst camp, worst training of any championship fight. But it's no excuse. I have no excuses. Yan beat me. I thought I could win and I took the fight, no regrets."

Dvalishvili's seemingly limitless capacity for work, pain and adversity has defined his career and endeared him to UFC fans. But that relentless drive can at times make the incredibly difficult sport of MMA even more challenging.

Dvalishvili's longtime training partner, former UFC bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling, told ESPN he admires Dvalishvili's pursuit of history last year -- but he never thought it was a sound idea.

"I knew we were in trouble coming out of the gate," Sterling said. "I didn't have a good feeling about it. I honestly wasn't even as involved in that fourth camp, because I didn't think we were taking the fight. I had scheduled a few other commitments because I thought we were done for the year.

"You try to be as positive as you can be, but you're also like, 'I don't want to see my friend get hurt because we jumped into something we shouldn't have jumped into.'" Of course, it's impossible to determine beforehand how much is too much for someone such as Dvalishvili.

Wood, who has been in Dvalishvili's corner for more than five years, was certain it was too much in January 2025, when Dvalishvili was set to fight then-18-0 fighter Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC 311. A deep cut on Dvalishvili's leg developed staph infection during training camp, leading to what Wood described as one of the most unhealthy fight preparations he has ever been involved in. But Dvalishvili still went out and defeated Nurmagomedov in a five-round performance that earned him a fight of the night bonus. Dvalishvili rallied in the championship rounds to claim a decision.

"That's the fight I actually considered pulling him out of," Wood said. "He was so damaged in multiple ways for that one, and then went out there and performed like he did. Once he did that, he convinced me to really never question him again. In my mind, I was like, 'Oh s---, this guy really can do anything. He really is just a machine.'"

Dvalishvili's loss to Yan hasn't prompted a complete overhaul of the approach. He's still sparring 10 rounds in a single session, but it has refocused the camp in some ways.

Dvalishvili has said he needed a better game plan going into that fight. Perhaps, he said, the team overlooked Yan while in the midst of a 14-fight win streak that spanned eight years and included a physically dominant unanimous decision victory over Yan in their first career meeting. Dvalishvili logged a UFC record 49 takedown attempts in that March 2023 win.

The circumstances surrounding Dvalishvili and Yan's two fights combine for a complicated backdrop to the third meeting. They have spent 10 rounds together in the Octagon, but few conclusions can be drawn because of the opposite outcomes. After the first fight, both bantamweights said they competed through injuries, but Dvalishvili was the clear winner. Yan decisively won the second bout -- claiming four of five rounds on two judges' scorecards -- but Dvalishvili was presumably compromised. Ahead of the trilogy, Sterling said the team has worked on improving Dvalishvili's ground control, allowing him to use his notorious gas tank more efficiently.

"I don't feel like there was a lot of emphasis on that in his last few camps," Sterling said. "I think we've done a better job at tightening up his wrestling base. If he can do half of the things I do when it comes to controlling guys once he gets them to the floor, it's going to be scary, because then you've got that infinite amount of cardio on top of it. That's a dangerous combination."

Yan, who spent the first half of this year recovering from back surgery, said tactics and mental preparation -- more than any physical improvements (or better health) -- will decide Saturday's contest.

On that front, Yan considers he and his team to have a distinct edge. After the last fight, his coach, Kairat Nurmagambetov, unveiled a digital strategy tree he built that outlined a detailed plan for nearly every potential scenario Dvalishvili might try in the Octagon. In a recent interview, Yan revealed that Nurmagambetov has expanded the playbook for the trilogy fight.

"This fight will be decided by fight IQ, mental strength and which fighter makes better decisions," Yan told ESPN, through a translator. "The second fight, I beat him. In the third, I will do the same."

It's a simple, interesting way to put it: Which fighter will make better decisions?

For Dvalishvili, that's always a loaded question. His questionable decision-making has been well-documented over the years -- at times hilariously so and often in ways that seem specific to him. Is sparring 10 rounds a good decision? Is hiding an injury from your own team? Is jumping into a frozen lake head first, as Dvalishvili famously did in 2021?

The answer for Dvalishvili might be relative when compared to other fighters. Dvalishvili's mindset about work and his willingness to fight injured are unlikely to change, but the loss to Yan did make him rethink certain strategies.

Over the course of Dvalishvili's title reign, he shocked much of the MMA world by choosing to spar five rounds at full speed on the morning of his championship fights. He did so in December, before losing to Yan. When asked if he expects to continue that tradition, Dvalishvili admitted that is one specific quirk that is likely retired for good.

"I'm not going to spar this time," Dvalishvili said. "Especially against Petr Yan, I need all of my energy. When I did the five rounds before our last fight, that was probably a mistake. But I learned and now I will fix it. I felt good doing it, but I think there is a smarter way."

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: ALEXIA PUTELLAS
This result is not a surprise. Putellas is the clear favourite for the award, and our voters agreed.

Putellas enjoyed a dream end to her 14-year Barcelona career last season, captaining the club to a second Quadruple in three years, including lifting the Women's Champions League, before she moved to captain London City Lionesses, who are now third in the Women's Super League after five games.

Should Putellas actually win, she would earn her third Ballon d'Or award, joining former Barcelona teammate Aitana Bonmatí as its most frequent recipient.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Game 4 feels like a must-win -- but can Valkyries generate enough offense?
stories.summary: What changes must Golden State make to counter Angel Reese's determination and dominance in the WNBA Finals?
stories.byline: Kareem Copeland and Kendra Andrews and Alexa Philippou
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- The most consequential 40 minutes of the WNBA season arrives Saturday (1 p.m. ET) as the Atlanta Dream host the Golden State Valkyries in Game 4 of the Finals. The Dream lead the series 2-1, and a victory heavily tips the scales in their favor to secure the first championship in franchise history. A Valkyries win sends the series back to San Francisco all tied up in a scenario where anything could happen.

Golden State coach Natalie Nakase has remained upbeat despite her team struggling in areas that have been a strength all season. Coming off their best game of the Finals, the Dream get to host another game in Atlanta in front of a raucous crowd that was an unquestioned advantage Wednesday in Game 3.

"You want to finish the job," Dream coach Karl Smesko said. "You want to finish it. These are two great teams going at it, competing at a high level, and only one of us get to be champions. So that should be enough motivation for everybody."

Ahead of Saturday's pivotal meeting, ESPN evaluates what's on the line, how each team got here and what changes to expect when the series continues.

Is Game 4 a must-win for the Valkyries?

Kendra Andrews: Yes. It's as much of a must-win as a non-elimination game can be. With this being only the second year of a best-of-seven series in the WNBA Finals, there isn't any history to look at regarding coming back from a 3-1 deficit (the Aces swept the Mercury last year). However, even when it was a best-of-five series, no team in league history has ever trailed by multiple games and come back to win. In the NBA, only one team has come back from a 3-1 deficit in the Finals (2016 Cleveland Cavaliers). It is critical that Golden State wins Game 4 to tie the series as it shifts back to Ballhalla, which could provide an opportunity for the Valkyries to take back control. With how strong the Dream looked in Game 3, it's hard to imagine the Valkyries beating Atlanta three times in a row, so they must try to regain control of home-court advantage.

Kareem Copeland: Essentially. Kendra broke down the 3-1 history above, and that would put Golden State in a massive hole to climb out of. Not only is that a tough ask, but the Valkyries have yet to show they can score enough points to win three consecutive games against the Dream. They've averaged just 68 points per game and have yet to shoot 35% from the field in any of the Finals contests. That's an extremely hard way to win three in a row.

Alexa Philippou: While it feels like the pressure is on the Valkyries to win and avoid going down 3-1, Golden State guard Veronica Burton told reporters on Thursday that "it would be silly to overreact right now." Still, the Valkyries understand what's at stake heading into Saturday. "We continue to point out the things where we lack discipline and where we lack maybe paying attention to their personnel," Burton said. "We address that and not overreact but also understand that there is a major sense of urgency, and we can't necessarily wait for anything to change."

Luckily, as Nakase pointed out, Golden State has been great this season with its back against the wall, so the Valkyries will derive some confidence from that.

What is the biggest adjustment Golden State must make?

Copeland: Cleaning up turnovers. The Valkyries cannot continue to give up the ball at the rate they have in the past two games. They turned it over 19 times in Game 2 and 17 times in Game 3. The Dream promptly scored 24 and 22 points, respectively, off those turnovers. Atlanta's Rhyne Howard became the first player in league history to record five steals in consecutive Finals games. Golden State hasn't been able to produce enough offense to have so many empty possessions. Not only are they empty possessions, but they also spark a Dream offense that struggled itself in Games 1 and 2.

Andrews: I get that defense will always be Golden State's motor, and the Valkyries shouldn't change. They say their offense thrives off their defense because of how good they are in transition. However, they aren't stopping the Dream nearly enough. If they aren't making stops, they must find a way to generate more offense. After leading the league in points per possession in transition in the regular season, they are struggling mightily in this area.

The Valkyries have also always been isolation-heavy in how they like to score -- beating their defenders one-on-one -- and led the league in isolations during the regular season although their efficiency on those plays ranked in the middle of the pack. But in the Finals, they are averaging less than one point on their isolations. Gabby Williams has particularly struggled one-on-one (defended mostly by Jordin Canada). With their two main offensive tactics ineffective, the Valkyries need to find another way to get going.

Philippou: Since Game 3 ended, the Valkyries have spoken a lot about not being consistently disciplined but also about needing to operate more connectedly as a unit. Nakase has taken accountability in needing to come up with a more efficient, aggressive and clear game plan, and said she'd be seeking input from players in individual conversations.

While Cecilia Zandalasini and Janelle Salaun were much more impactful in Game 3, and Golden State had some success from beyond the arc with 12 triples, to Kendra's point, it'll be worth seeing whether the Valkyries can help Williams get going offensively. After her Game 1 heroics, she shot 30% or worse from the field in the next two games. Golden State needs her to snatch back the momentum and lead in this series.

Has the Valkyries' No. 1-rated defense sputtered or has Atlanta's offense just been too good?

Copeland: That defense didn't sputter until Wednesday, when the Dream shot 49.3% from the field and scored the second-most points the Valkyries have allowed in regulation this postseason. Game 3 was certainly ugly as Angel Reese continued to dominate and Rhyne Howard and Naz Hillmon started knocking down 3-pointers. But Atlanta shot just 33.9% in Game 2 and 32.8% in Game 1. The Golden State defense has been stout in two of three games, but those aforementioned turnovers gifted the Dream a ton of free points that have been the difference in the two Valkyries losses.

Philippou: It's not a great sign for Golden State that the Dream have scored progressively more points in each game of this series: 64 in Game 1, 79 in Game 2 and 97 in Game 3. And that's all without Howard having a great postseason shootingwise -- she has shot above 40% from the floor in only one playoff game and went sub-30% from the field in Games 1 and 2 of the Finals.

The Valkyries have allowed Atlanta to thrive in transition the past two games, and they haven't done a great job of generating Dream turnovers that they could score off. But they've had no real answer for Reese across Games 2 and 3. She's averaging 21.7 points -- on 56.4% shooting -- 13.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.0 blocks in the series. The Dream go as she goes.

What has been the biggest difference in Angel Reese's game since the start of the season?

Copeland: Her determination. Reese not only believes there isn't anyone on the Valkyries who can slow her down, but she's forcing the issue -- in a good way. Her confidence level is sky high at the moment and she knows her teammates feed off it. You see it when Reese snatches a rebound and goes coast-to-coast in her 6-foot-4 frame against the league's No. 1 defense without a care in the world.

The biggest example might have been when she had the ball at the top of the arc, gave a jab step and then rose up to knock down a triple without hesitation. That's supreme confidence for someone who had a combined seven 3-pointers in her first two WNBA seasons. Reese said it herself: That mindset and approach has been contagious for her teammates.

Philippou: Much has been made about Reese's will to win, but Smesko also credited Reese's hard work during the season, saying "she very well might be the most improved player from the beginning of the season to right now." Reese has been working on improving her outside shot with Smesko and refining her post work with assistant coach LaToya Sanders. Reese shot 42.5% from the field before the All-Star break versus 48.4% afterward, and now 48.1% in the postseason. Per GeniusIQ, Reese's qSI -- a stat measuring effective field goal percentage minus the expected effective field goal percentage on the shot -- has jumped from minus-3.6 before the FIBA break (meaning her effective field goal percentage was 4.1% worse than expected) to 6.0 since.

She has also made 8 of 17 (47.1%) 3-pointers in the playoffs versus 3 of 25 (12%) pre-All-Star break and 8 of 32 (25%) post-All-Star break.

stories.headline: Liverpool's Andoni Iraola urges Rio Ngumoha not to be distracted by 'outside noise'
stories.summary: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has urged Rio Ngumoha not to be distracted by the outside noise following his impressive performance against Villarreal.
stories.body:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has urged Rio Ngumoha not to be distracted by the outside noise following his impressive performance against Villarreal.

Ngumoha was the Reds' standout performer on Tuesday night as they came from 2-0 down to beat the Spanish side 4-3 in the Champions League at Anfield.

The England international admitted after the match that it was "one of his best" displays for the club but Iraola has stressed the importance of his players not getting caught up in any external attention.

"I think every player has to focus on performances, on keeping doing well and improve the things he can improve," Iraola said in a news conference on Friday.

"The outside noise, when it's good, when it's bad I think it affects -- obviously -- but we have to not be affected by those things.

"You continue to do your job, as good as you can, try to improve the things you can improve and don't be too affected from the things you can hear.

"When you do well they are going to praise you, when you do bad they are going to be critics but don't let those things affect too much the performance, which in the end is the most important thing.

- Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or-worthy goalscoring numbers: What stats, charts say

- As Anthony Gordon prepares for El Clásico debut, how have other British stars fared?

- Antonio Conte, Fabian Hürzeler distance themselves from Man United job

"Not just with Rio, with everyone, it's about feeling how they are. We change the team a lot because we play every three to four days.

"Sometimes players are tired and there is more risk involved so we have to decide if they need more rest or we use more fresh legs. It will be the same in the coming games."

Liverpool will return to Premier League action on Sunday when they host high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion.

Bradley Barcola has been passed fit to play after missing team training on Thursday but Iraola could be without some key players against Fabian Hurzeler's side.

"Bradley has trained today as normal," Iraola said. "No problem, it was just a matter of sometimes we just have to deal with the workloads but he is fine.

"Victor [Munoz] had a knock in the first half against Brentford. He could finish the game very well but he is dealing with some pain since then. It was too early against Villarreal and I think it's going to be difficult [to play against Brighton] but I don't know.

"Dom [Szoboszlai] is going to be out this weekend. I don't think he's far but he hasn't trained with the group still and also considering that [against Brentford] we started him and he had to go out, we will probably take one or two days more than we would last week.

"He's in a good place. Dom is already training outside alone and he's going to train with the group but he's not ready for this one."

stories.headline: UFC 333 preview and picks for featherweight, men's bantamweight titles
stories.summary: Check out the matchups and expert predictions for both championship fights at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
How does a fighter know when to stop when they're fighting well?

It's a question that, unfortunately, rarely gets answered in MMA. For every athlete who retires from the sport on their own terms, there are at least two athletes being retired by the sport. It is rare for a fighter to go out on a win, and infinitely rare for a fighter to go out on top.

UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski (28-4) is starting to look that question in the face. Volkanovski will look to defend his title at UFC 333 on Saturday against 32-year-old Movsar Evloev (20-0) in Abu Dhabi, UAE. Volkanovski, 38, already is defying the rules of Father Time. In April 2025, he became the first fighter older than 35 to win a UFC championship belt in a weight class under 170 pounds. He defended that title in January against 31-year-old Diego Lopes.

In the past, Volkanovski has been dismissive, even comedic, of his age, starring in self-deprecating "Old Man Volk" skits on the internet. Ahead of UFC 333, however, he's been discussing age far more seriously, saying that any fight moving forward could be his last.

"There's a reason this is not often done," Volkanovski told ESPN. "I will bring up [my age], because I think it adds to the story. A lot of people are thinking about it. The young, undefeated guy -- facing the old, 38-year-old."

Evloev, of Russia, is one of the most proven title challengers in featherweight division history, with a perfect 10-0 record inside the Octagon, but he hasn't finished a single UFC opponent. He is a slight underdog against Volkanovski, according to DraftKings -- a credit to how good Volkanovski has looked, as well as lingering doubts on Evloev's ceiling.

Volkanovski, a two-time champion who suffered back-to-back knockout losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria before regaining his title in 2025, told ESPN he believes he will actually look better than ever on Saturday, due to Evloev's style. The undefeated challenger is known primarily as a position-focused grappler, who might struggle to match Volkanovski's striking and scrambling ability.

"His style is a perfect matchup for me, I truly believe that," Volkanovski said. "I'm not delusional, saying I'm the best I've ever been at age 38. I'm not in my prime. But stylistically, I think you guys will be saying, 'I swear this is the best Volk we've ever seen.'"

Even if that is the case, odds say Volkanovski is tempting fate with every performance from this point forward. Male UFC fighters 38 and older have won 37% of their bouts all time, according to ESPN Research. Volkanovski has acknowledged as much and even proposed a "sendoff" title fight against 37-year-old lightweight champion Justin Gaethje next, after which they would both retire.

Volkanovski has stated he's taking it one fight at a time, but he is talking about retirement now, which shows he understands the decision is in front of him.

"One hundred percent, if I notice I'm slowing down or I'm taking more damage, [I'll retire]," Volkanovski said. "I said that before my last fight, too. A lot of people look at me saying that and say, 'Look how he's talking, his head isn't in it.' I'm just real and I'm honest. I said it before my last fight, and what happened? I went out there and made it look easy."

More storylines to watch

Dvalishvili looks to prove the last fight was an outlier
Merab Dvalishvili attempted to make history at the end of 2025, when he fought Petr Yan in his fourth men's bantamweight title defense of the calendar year. The feat has never been accomplished -- or even attempted -- and it proved to be too much as Dvalishvili lost a five-round decision. He later revealed he went into the bout with a significant knee injury and had a terrible camp. Dvalishvili (21-5) will try to recapture his title against Yan (20-5) in the UFC 333 co-main event.

Although he's admitted to tough circumstances around their last meeting, Dvalishvili has also said he doesn't regret pursuing UFC history and won't use those circumstances as an excuse, crediting Yan for the victory.

But the fighters' shared history has obviously raised the stakes for this Saturday. Dvalishvili and Yan have met twice, with Dvalishvili dominating their first meeting in March 2023. If Yan wins the trilogy, against a much fresher version of Dvalishvili than he saw in December, it could push Dvalishvili toward the back of the line for another title shot.

Not the last chance, but kind of the last chance
Not to put unnecessary pressure onto Aaron Pico's shoulders, but the truth is that any type of loss to Losene Keita -- a promising talent who is only 1-1 in the UFC -- would have heavy, long-lasting implications.

Pico, 30, has won 10 of his past 12 fights, but this is still a crossroads. He's been viewed as championship material since before his professional MMA debut, but has endured violent, memorable setbacks at various points in his career, including a spinning back elbow knockout loss to Lerone Murphy in his UFC debut 14 months ago. There is still massive potential in Pico, and he had an impressive bounce-back win against Patricio Pitbull in April, but he's in a risky position this weekend. He faces a dangerous but relatively unknown opponent in Keita after his original opponent, Arnold Allen, was forced off the card. Saturday's outcome will go a long way in determining how matchmakers and fans view him moving forward.

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Can Evloev significantly control Volkanovski on the ground?
Evloev is good everywhere, but Volkanovski has such an ability to game plan and show up in the big moments. Evloev is super big and strong. He has good standup, great transitions and ground control. But Volkanovski was able to get up after being taken down by Islam Makhachev. Are we just gonna forget that? Islam is now a welterweight. Volkanovski is so intelligent and so good at finding ways to exploit guys. His fight IQ is as good as anyone I've ever watched. He showed it against Lopes in their rematch in January. If Evloev cannot control Volk on the ground for long periods of time, Volkanovski will win a decision. And with the modern emphasis on damage when it comes to scoring, judges don't want to see you unsuccessfully try to hold someone down. Volkanovski by decision. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Will age catch up to Volkanovski?
The biggest X factor is that unknown: At what point does Volkanovski's age slow him down? He's fighting one of the purest wrestlers/grapplers in the UFC in Evloev. I could see Evloev trying to prove he can stand with Volkanovski at times and win over the UFC, but I don't think that would be his smartest decision. Personally, I believe that "Old Man Volk" still has it. He's proven time and again he's going to win those key wrestling scrambles, and I believe he'll end up catching Movsar. It will be a grinder of a fight, but Volkanovski's experience being in there with bigger, stronger guys like Islam will pay off. Volkanovski by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Can Dvavishvili hurt Yan with his hands?
We know that Yan has the physicality to compete with Merab's wrestling. He didn't avoid the takedown in their last fight -- he actually got more takedowns than Merab. That's a fact. And Yan on the feet is so dangerous, you have to give his standup the edge. If he comes in in great shape and can counter-wrestle and have the same physicality he did in December, he can win. The biggest technical question is whether Merab can create enough offense to get inside and hurt Yan with his hands. If the wrestling gets shut down, can he create offense? If Merab can hurt Yan on the feet, that changes the whole fight and throws it in favor of Merab. I've got Yan winning by a slight edge. -- Saud

Who will control the resets?
Yan needs to control the range, punish Merab's entries and continually invest in the body. He needs to establish the center and force Merab to initiate his wrestling from a distance, and intersect those entries with straight punches, body shots and uppercuts. I'd like to see him keep that lead arm frame, to establish his underhooks right away with his wrestling defense. He doesn't need to eliminate the takedown attempt, but he does need to make Merab pay for every failed attempt. Merab, meanwhile, has to weaponize pace, create chaos and disrupt Yan's comfort. He has to chain together multiple takedown attempts, so that even failed attempts affect Yan's rhythm. Who will control the resets? Merab thrives when one attack becomes three or four; Yan thrives when he's able to reset and return to technical striking. I lean Yan by decision again. --Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: NHL Power Rankings: Fantasy hockey pickups for all 32 teams
stories.summary: The Hurricanes hang on to the No. 1 spot, with some major jumbles in the poll thereafter.
stories.body:
Another week, another No. 1 spot in our poll for the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. But while there was no change at the top, there were substantial changes from Nos. 2 to 32 this week.

Plus, do you need help maximizing your fantasy hockey team's chances?

You're in luck, because Sean Allen (Eastern Conference) and Victoria Matiash (Western Conference) are here to identify one worthwhile pickup for all 32 clubs.

And a reminder: It's not too late to play ESPN Fantasy Hockey, with new leagues starting every Monday.

How we rank: A panel of ESPN hockey commentators, analysts, reporters and editors sends in a 1-32 poll based on the games through Wednesday. Those ballots are combined to come up with the rankings you see below.

Note: Previous ranking for each team refers to the previous edition, published on Oct. 16. Points percentages are through Thursday's games.

1. Carolina Hurricanes
Previous ranking: 1

Points percentage: 75%

Jaccob Slavin, D, (1.67 fantasy points per game, 67.3% available in ESPN leagues): Slavin has 18 fantasy points without a goal or any real power-play time. That's a floor built on peripherals and a 10-6 edge at 5-on-5 for a Carolina team allowing just 22.4 shots a game. Long a real-hockey darling, he's finally paying off in fantasy, too.

Next seven days: @ STL (Oct. 24), vs. BOS (Oct. 27), vs. CBJ (Oct. 29)

2. Edmonton Oilers
Previous ranking: 3

Points percentage: 85%

Devon Levi, G (2.72 FPPG, 61.5% available): Toss out the first two games of the season under new coach Mike Babcock, and the Oilers are icing the second-best defense in the NHL. For which Levi deserves some personal credit through six appearances, as made evident by his 4.82 goals saved above expected (GSAx) metric, according to Evolving Hockey.

Next seven days: vs. TOR (Oct. 24), vs. DET (Oct. 26), vs. CGY (Oct. 28)

3. Vegas Golden Knights
Previous ranking: 2

Points percentage: 66.67%

Adin Hill, G (3.91 FPPG, 78.6% available): After stumbling through 2025-26, the Vegas netminder looks back to his old solid self. Carrying a 4-0 record and 2.21 GAA into Thursday, Hill has been better than Carter Hart to date. It might not be too long before he gets more opportunities to backstop one of the best teams in the West.

Next seven days: @ CBJ (Oct. 24), vs. OTT (Oct. 27)

4. Tampa Bay Lightning
Previous ranking: 9

Points percentage: 77.78%

Charle-Edouard D'Astous, D (1.54 FPPG, 96.8% available): D'Astous just earned a promotion worth noticing, as he has been on the ice for most of the Lightning's power-play time over the past two games. A defender with top-unit access on a contender is worth a speculative add, especially at barely 3% rostered.

Next seven days: @ COL (Oct. 23), @ UTA (Oct. 24), vs. WPG (Oct. 29)

5. Boston Bruins
Previous ranking: 7

Points percentage: 77.27%

James Hagens, C (1.94 FPPG, 86.8% available): Hagens is doing a lot with a little. The rookie is averaging under 13 minutes a night, yet he has three goals in 10 games while skating with Elias Lindholm and Casey Mittelstadt lately, and Boston has outscored opponents 7-3 at 5-on-5 with him on the ice. More ice time is the only thing missing.

Next seven days: vs. SJ (Oct. 24), @ CAR (Oct. 27), @ STL (Oct. 29)

6. Utah Mammoth
Previous ranking: 4

Points percentage: 63.64%

Kailer Yamamoto, RW (2.32 FPPG, 95.1% available): The winger is off to a hot start with two goals and three assists in five games. Will this sizzling trend last? Absolutely not. But there's still fantasy value to mine from Yamamoto in the meanwhile, as long as he's seeing valuable minutes alongside Barrett Hayton and Anders Lee 5-on-5 and with the extra skater.

Next seven days: vs. TB (Oct. 24), vs. MIN (Oct. 27), @ PIT (Oct. 29)

7. New York Rangers
Previous ranking: 5

Points percentage: 62.5%

Gabe Perreault, RW (1.75 FPPG, 65.9% available): Perreault has settled in with Mika Zibanejad and Alexis Lafreniere, and the trio has yet to be scored on at 5-on-5 (4-0 in 96 minutes together). He's at 1.88 FPPG over his past 10 games and is still available in about two-thirds of leagues.

Next seven days: @ OTT (Oct. 24), vs. LA (Oct. 26)

8. Minnesota Wild
Previous ranking: 8

Points percentage: 63.64%

Jared Spurgeon, D (2.40 FPPG lately, 72.8% available): Expected to make his return soon, Spurgeon once again projects to fill a prominent role on a blue line that's missing Brock Faber for the foreseeable future. Before suffering an upper-body injury, the veteran defender punched out five points, seven shots, and 14 blocked shots in six contests.

Next seven days: @ SEA (Oct. 24), @ VAN (Oct. 25), @ UTA (Oct. 27), vs. NYI (Oct. 29)

9. Ottawa Senators
Previous ranking: 12

Points percentage: 63.64%

Tyler Kleven, D (2.03 FPPG, 75.5% available): Kleven is producing like a top fantasy defender without a whiff of power-play time, logging more than 21 minutes a night and lately pairing with Jordan Spence. Expect some cooling, but peripheral-driven production tends to hold better than a hot shooting streak.

Next seven days: vs. NYR (Oct. 24), @ VGK (Oct. 27), @ LA (Oct. 29)

10. Dallas Stars
Previous ranking: 17

Points percentage: 65%

David Perron, RW (N/A FPPG, 99.8% available): A true fantasy wild card, the veteran winger signed with the Stars only days ago. If he eventually carves out a spot in the top six and secures a role on the power play, Perron could prove productive enough to deserve a spot on deeper fantasy rosters. Since Dallas ranks in the bottom quarter in league scoring, coach Glen Gulutzan is guaranteed to at least give the 38-year-old opportunities.

Next seven days: vs. NYI (Oct. 25), vs. NJ (Oct. 27), vs. MTL (Oct. 29)

11. Florida Panthers
Previous ranking: 13

Points percentage: 54.55%

Eetu Luostarinen, LW (1.21 FPPG, 97.6% available): Slim pickings in Florida. Luostarinen's selling point is the role: nearly 16 minutes a night alongside Anton Lundell and Sandis Vilmanis, plus second-unit power-play time. He's a deep-league play, but he's available almost everywhere.

Next seven days: @ CHI (Oct. 25), @ WPG (Oct. 27)

12. Colorado Avalanche
Previous ranking: 6

Points percentage: 55%

Gabriel Landeskog, LW (1.77 FPPG, 70.8% available): Skating on a second line and secondary power play, Colorado's captain boasts a rather quiet haul of three goals in his most recent string of four games. It might not be long before coach Jared Bednar has Landeskog back on his top unit with the extra skater in lieu of rookie T.J. Hughes.

Next seven days: vs. TB (Oct. 23), @ NSH (Oct. 25), vs. NJ (Oct. 28)

13. Seattle Kraken
Previous ranking: 10

Points percentage: 68.18%

Jordan Eberle, RW (2.11 FPPG, 41.9% available): On a Kraken team that scores by committee, Eberle is kicking in his fair share at even strength and with the extra skater. Competing on a top unit and No. 1 power play with Jared McCann, Eberle provides bonus fantasy points with shots on goal and blocked shots. It all adds up.

Next seven days: vs. MIN (Oct. 24), vs. TOR (Oct. 28)

14. New York Islanders
Previous ranking: 22

Points percentage: 60%

Logan Stanley, D (1.58 FPPG, 86.7% available): Riding shotgun with Matthew Schaefer has its perks. Stanley is logging 20:45 a night next to the rookie, and the Islanders have outscored opponents 4-1 at 5-on-5 with the pair together. His job is to keep the puck out, which drives a steady source of plus-minus for fantasy managers.

Next seven days: @ DAL (Oct. 25), @ NSH (Oct. 27), @ MIN (Oct. 29)

15. Washington Capitals
Previous ranking: 15

Points percentage: 55.56%

Ryan Leonard, RW (1.97 FPPG, 64.9% available): Leonard's even-strength role is modest -- barely 14 minutes a night -- but Washington has him on the ice for 57% of its power-play time. Four goals in nine games with limited ice shows what he can do, and the ceiling rises with every minute added.

Next seven days: vs. BUF (Oct. 24), vs. PHI (Oct. 28), @ NSH (Oct. 29)

16. Toronto Maple Leafs
Previous ranking: 19

Points percentage: 58.33%

Easton Cowan, LW/RW (1.94 FPPG, 61.3% available): Toronto kept shuffling Cowan through the lineup, and he kept producing anyway, with four goals in 11 games and just over 2.0 FPPG across his last 10. Now he has landed alongside Auston Matthews, which is when the floor really starts to rise.

Next seven days: @ EDM (Oct. 24), @ CGY (Oct. 26), @ SEA (Oct. 28)

17. New Jersey Devils
Previous ranking: 23

Points percentage: 60%

Arseny Gritsyuk, LW/RW (1.93 FPPG, 96.1% available): Gritsyuk has landed the best seat in New Jersey, flanking Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes for most of his even-strength minutes. He has four goals in nine games, and he's still unclaimed in 96% of leagues. That won't last if he keeps that seat.

Next seven days: vs. LA (Oct. 24), @ DAL (Oct. 27), @ COL (Oct. 28)

18. Winnipeg Jets
Previous ranking: 11

Points percentage: 55%

Neal Pionk, D (2.01 FPPG, 57.0% available): While Josh Morrissey remains sidelined week-to-week, Pionk is saddled with the task of anchoring the Jets' No. 1 power play. Skating on the top pair, he also answers the initial call on the penalty kill. It all adds up to a lot of minutes and opportunities to rack up valuable fantasy points. The Winnipeg defender warrants rostering in all but the shallowest of leagues.

Next seven days: vs. MTL (Oct. 25), vs. FLA (Oct. 27), @ TB (Oct. 29)

19. Montreal Canadiens
Previous ranking: 21

Points percentage: 55.56%

Jacob Fowler, G (3.35 FPPG lately, 75.0% available): Fowler has started three of Montreal's past five games and is averaging 3.35 fantasy points in that stretch. A .901 save percentage says it isn't all smooth, but a young goalie pushing for the crease is worth stashing, and he's still on the wire in three out of four leagues.

Next seven days: @ CHI (Oct. 23), @ WPG (Oct. 25), @ STL (Oct. 27), @ DAL (Oct. 29)

20. Nashville Predators
Previous ranking: 25

Points percentage: 50%

Adam Edstrom, LW (2.44 FPPG, 76.7% available): Never mind the limited ice time, Edstrom ranks in the top five in hits per game and top 10 in blocked shots by forwards. Toss in a healthy number of shots and goals, as well as his proclivity for short-handed points, and the new Predator is well worth acquiring in leagues that reward physical play.

Next seven days: @ PIT (Oct. 24), vs. COL (Oct. 25), vs. NYI (Oct. 27), vs. WSH (Oct. 29)

21. St. Louis Blues
Previous ranking: 16

Points percentage: 55%

Jimmy Snuggerud, RW (1.83 FPPG, 70.1% available): After amassing 36 points in his final 31 games of his rookie campaign, the 22-year-old projects to flirt with the 40-goal mark this season. Competing on a top line and power play with Robert Thomas and Dylan Holloway, Snuggerud is off to a good start with five goals in nine.

Next seven days: vs. CAR (Oct. 24), vs. MTL (Oct. 27), vs. BOS (Oct. 29)

22. San Jose Sharks
Previous ranking: 24

Points percentage: 59.09%

Ivar Stenberg, LW (1.57 FPPG, 61.1% available): Fantasy managers are quickly becoming smitten with this year's No. 2 draft pick. After a slightly quieter start, the (just-turned) 19-year-old rookie is finding his rhythm, averaging 2.32 fantasy points per game in five recent contests. Skating on a top power play with Macklin Celebrini is also a promising assignment.

Next seven days: @ BOS (Oct. 24), vs. BUF (Oct. 27), vs. VAN (Oct. 29)

23. Buffalo Sabres
Previous ranking: 20

Points percentage: 50%

Jack Quinn, RW (2.20 FPPG, 44.7% available): Quinn just crossed the 50% rostered mark, so if he's still out there in your league, move now. He's skating nearly 20 minutes a night on a line that has been dominant at 5-on-5 and soaking up most of Buffalo's power-play time. Too late? Linemate Zach Benson is available almost everywhere.

Next seven days: @ WSH (Oct. 24), @ SJ (Oct. 27), @ ANA (Oct. 29)

24. Anaheim Ducks
Previous ranking: 14

Points percentage: 40%

Mikael Granlund, C/LW (2.10 FPPG, 31.1% available): More offense from the Ducks needs to come from somewhere. After Cutter Gauthier, Leo Carlsson, and Beckett Sennecke -- all widely rostered -- that responsibility must largely fall to the club's veteran center. Before missing a game with a minor upper-body injury, Granlund collected two goals and six assists, including four points on the power play, through six contests. The 34-year-old also blocks more shots than your average forward.

Next seven days: @ PHI (Oct. 24), vs. VAN (Oct. 27), vs. BUF (Oct. 29)

25. Detroit Red Wings
Previous ranking: 27

Points percentage: 55%

Viktor Arvidsson, RW (1.96 FPPG, 74.4% available): Arvidsson's value runs through the power play: 4:00 a night and 63% of Detroit's time with the advantage. Even strength has been rough, but he's spending most of those shifts with Dylan Larkin and Lucas Raymond lately, and four goals in nine games says the chances are coming.

Next seven days: @ CGY (Oct. 24), @ EDM (Oct. 26), vs. CHI (Oct. 29)

26. Pittsburgh Penguins
Previous ranking: 18

Points percentage: 40.91%

Declan Carlile, D (2.03 FPPG, 57.0% available): Three goals from a defender with no power-play time is rare, and Carlile has 20 fantasy points in 10 games playing almost 19 minutes a night. The goals will slow, and he has been on the ice for plenty of action at both ends, but the minutes make him a solid floor play.

Next seven days: vs. NSH (Oct. 24), vs. UTA (Oct. 29)

27. Columbus Blue Jackets
Previous ranking: 26

Points percentage: 37.5%

Cole Sillinger, LW/RW (1.77 FPPG, 93.7% available): Columbus is sputtering, but Sillinger isn't. He has three goals in eight games while skating alongside Charlie Coyle and Mathieu Olivier, and he's doing it with barely any power-play time. Available in nearly every league, adding him is a cheap bet on a forward who's producing without the perks.

Next seven days: vs. VGK (Oct. 24), @ PHI (Oct. 27), @ CAR (Oct. 29)

28. Philadelphia Flyers
Previous ranking: 32

Points percentage: 37.5%

Nick Seeler, D (1.75 FPPG, 83.8% available): Someone has to deal with all those shots. The Flyers get outshot most nights, and Seeler, at nearly 20 minutes a night beside Jamie Drysdale, has turned the chaos into steady fantasy value almost entirely through peripherals. Ugly team, useful floor.

Next seven days: vs. ANA (Oct. 24), vs. CBJ (Oct. 27), @ WSH (Oct. 28)

29. Chicago Blackhawks
Previous ranking: 28

Points percentage: 33.33%

Frank Nazar, C (1.53 FPPG, 85.4% available): There's so much scoring potential with this young skater. After collecting 41 points through 66 games last season, Nazar is expected to take another step forward. Three goals in the span of four contests -- interrupted by a short suspension -- suggests the 22-year-old is already on track for an improving Blackhawks squad.

Next seven days: vs. MTL (Oct. 23), vs. FLA (Oct. 25), vs. LA (Oct. 27), @ DET (Oct. 29)

30. Los Angeles Kings
Previous ranking: 29

Points percentage: 37.5%

Darcy Kuemper, G (-1.3 FPPG, 52.9% available): Under new coach Peter Laviolette, the Kings are better than their early-season record suggests. Now that Mats Zuccarello is back in the lineup, and Kevin Fiala is eyeing a return in early November, more wins will start to pile up shortly. Plus, after his atrocious opener in Colorado, Kuemper has been altogether solid for Los Angeles.

Next seven days: @ NJ (Oct. 24), @ NYR (Oct. 26), @ CHI (Oct. 27), vs. OTT (Oct. 29)

31. Calgary Flames
Previous ranking: 31

Points percentage: 33.33%

Matt Coronato, RW (1.40 FPPG, 74.1% available): There's a lot of pressure on the Flames' highest-paid active forward (while Jonathan Huberdeau lingers on IR) to help his squad remain competitive in games on a nightly basis. Following a sluggish start, Coronato has upped his production with a goal and three helpers in four matches leading into Thursday. His enduring roles on Calgary's top line and power play hint at more productive days ahead. On a roster bereft of fantasy talent, the 23-year-old at least merits monitoring.

Next seven days: vs. DET (Oct. 24), vs. TOR (Oct. 26), @ EDM (Oct. 28)

Previous ranking: 30

Points percentage: 20.83%

Elias N. Pettersson, D (1.88 FPPG, 72.4% available): He blocks a lot of pucks and throws a lot of hits. The odd goal is nice, too. While the club's other Elias Pettersson leads the (limited) fantasy parade in Vancouver, the same-named blueliner ranks third among skaters with 20.7 points through 11 contests.
